title: Crash Reporting, Breadcrumbs, and Correlation Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies crash reporting, breadcrumbs, and correlation?
options: Capture exact release context and bounded safe breadcrumbs, then prioritise grouped issues by affected users and user impact.
Count every validation error as non-fatal
Assume two tools use the same population
questions.answer: Capture exact release context and bounded safe breadcrumbs, then prioritise grouped issues by affected users and user impact.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: Crashlytics and Android vitals should always report identical crash rates for the same release.
questions.explanation: Recording every caught exception as non-fatal creates noise, consumes quotas, and can hide the few failures that need engineering action.

questions.prompt: Why must mappings and symbols match the exact build?
questions.answer: Optimisation and linking change names and addresses per artifact, so nearby-build metadata can produce a false stack diagnosis.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
